text:
maya: FYI I dragged my whole setup onto the balcony this morning. sun is great, plants are cheering me on, but my wifi and I are not on speaking terms. anyone have a weatherproof mesh or hotspot setup rec? :sweat_smile:
aj: pics or it didn't happen :grin:
maya: https://imgur.com/a/abcd123 - cable management is a crime scene but look at the light :sun_with_face:
chris: powerline adapters work surprisingly well if your apartment wiring isn't ancient. cheap and quick.
nina: +1 to Ubiquiti Mesh if you can run a tiny PoE switch near the balcony. survived a thunderstorm for us.
leo: quick unscientific poll: react with :deciduous_tree: for balcony, :sun_with_face: for window desk, :umbrella: for 'I will never trust outdoor ethernet'
ops-bot: Automated reminder: Please avoid exposing customer data in public images. If that board behind you has any sticky notes with tickets, blur before posting. :lock:
maya: good call ops-bot, cleaned the board. posted a trimmed pic now. thx.
sam: speedtest from balcony (over 5GHz ext):
```
Ping: 42 ms
Download: 17.8 Mbps
Upload: 5.2 Mbps
```
not great for video calls but fine for async work. anyone tried running a small LTE router as backup?
aj: i used an old phone as hotspot during an outage. pro tip: put it on a mini tripod and clip a little foam behind for airflow, battery lasts longer. :battery:
chris: if you want to get fancy, a cheap LTE router + external antenna + a battery pack will keep you online through a storm. but that's kinda overkill unless you're streaming plants. :joy:
maya: appreciate the tips. plan: try powerline tonight, if that fails i'll spring for a tiny LTE router. will report back with before/after pics and maybe a 'balcony office survival' thread. :thumbsup:
